habitat: Mostly singly in a variety of wooded habitats, including rural suburbia.
summary: A common resident. Dark grey-brown above, with white eyebrows and a white throat marked by black moustachial streaks. The upper breast is greyish, the flanks are washed orange and the belly is white. The eye-ring, bill and legs are orange. At dusk it calls peet-peeoo, and it also has a mellow song. The page uses Turdus libonyanus. This list keeps Turdus libonyana. The immature is only said to be as illustrated. The Kemp name Kurrichane Thrush and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Olive Thrush has orange underparts and a speckled throat, without Kurrichane’s black-and-white throat markings and white eyebrows.

head.pattern: White eyebrows and a white throat with black moustachial streaks.

underparts.pattern: Upper breast greyish. Flanks washed orange.

calls.description: A loud 'peet-peeoo' at dusk, and a mellow song of trills and warbles in short outbursts. The grade A call is from Kruger. The filename is XC237783-1007_cut.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. Dark grey-brown and greyish are not stored as single colours. The immature is only said to be as illustrated. The page spells the name Turdus libonyanus. The grade A call is from Kruger. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.
